newsitem.title: USA: ICN says forex, weak Virazole sales cut Q1.
newsitem.headline: ICN says forex, weak Virazole sales cut Q1.

text.p: ICN Pharmaceuticals Inc said first quarter net income per share fell below year-ago levels because of lower sales of its drug Virazole in North America and foreign exchange losses.
The company said quarterly net income fell to $0.50 compared to $0.65. It said the lower Virazole shares cut earnings per share by $0.12 and foreign exchange losses cut EPS by $0.08 a share.
Net income rose slightly to $22.3 million compared to $22.0 million with a higher number of shares outstanding.
Wall Street analysts had estimated ICN would earn $0.71 in the first quarter on average, according to First Call.

Virazole is used to treat infants hospitalized with severe respiratory tract infections caused by respiratory syncytial virus. The drug was the subject of a class action lawsuit which was settled in October.
Research and development expenditures for the quarter rose 22 percent compared to the prior year quarter, it said.
At its Yugoslavia business, sales fell to $51.0 million compared to $61.8 million last year although operating income grew to $19.3 million from $10.5 million last year.

ICN said it cut its net monetary asset exposure in Yugoslavia from $134.0 million at the beginning of the year to $47.0 million as of March 31, 1997, by converting $80.0 million of dinar denominated accounts receivable into notes receivable that are fixed in dollar amounts.
It will convert an additional $20.0 million of accounts receivable in the second quarter.

Sales and operating income at the company's Russia and Hungary operations grew but North American first quarter pharmaceuticals sales were sharply lower at $22.3 million compared to $31.1 million in the first quarter last year. Operating income for the same period was $8.3 million versus $16.4 million last year in North America.
